segments.speaker: WOMAN
segments.en: Good evening. King’s Restaurant.

segments.speaker: MAN
segments.en: Good evening. I’m ringing about the job I understand you have vacant.

segments.speaker: WOMAN
segments.en: Oh yes.

segments.speaker: MAN
segments.en: I’d like to find out a few more details, if I may.

segments.speaker: WOMAN
segments.en: Yes, of course. Can I take your name?

segments.speaker: MAN
segments.en: It’s Peter Chin.

segments.speaker: WOMAN
segments.en: Okay, Peter. Well, if you want to ask about the job and then if we’re both still interested, we could arrange for you to come for an interview.

segments.speaker: MAN
segments.en: Great, thanks. I’m afraid I missed the advert for the job but heard about it from a friend.

segments.speaker: WOMAN
segments.en: That’s no problem at all. What would you like to know?

segments.speaker: MAN
segments.en: Well, um, what sort of work is it – washing up?

segments.speaker: WOMAN
segments.en: It’s answering the phone [[ ]] .

segments.speaker: MAN
segments.en: Oh right, fine.

segments.speaker: WOMAN
segments.en: And not waiting at table.

segments.speaker: MAN
segments.en: That’d be good. And how many nights a week would it be?

segments.speaker: WOMAN
segments.en: Well, we’re really only busy at the weekend.

segments.speaker: MAN
segments.en: So two nights?

segments.speaker: WOMAN
segments.en: Three actually, so it would work out at twelve hours a week.

segments.speaker: MAN
segments.en: That’d be fine. It wouldn’t interfere with my studies.

segments.speaker: WOMAN
segments.en: Are you at the university?

segments.speaker: MAN
segments.en: Yes. First-year Physics student.

segments.speaker: WOMAN
segments.en: Oh, right.

segments.speaker: MAN
segments.en: Um, and because I’m not an EU national would I need a work permit?

segments.speaker: WOMAN
segments.en: Yes, you would. Just get your tutor to sign it.

segments.speaker: MAN
segments.en: That wouldn’t be a problem if I were to get the job. Um, where exactly is the restaurant?

segments.speaker: WOMAN
segments.en: Well, we have two branches – the one we’re recruiting for is in Hillsdunne Road [[ ]] .

segments.speaker: MAN
segments.en: I don’t know that. How do you spell it, please?

segments.speaker: WOMAN
segments.en: It’s H-I-double L-S-D-U-double N-E Road.

segments.speaker: MAN
segments.en: Got that. Thanks. Is it near a bus stop?

segments.speaker: WOMAN
segments.en: Yes. The nearest one would probably be just beside the Library [[ ]] .

segments.speaker: MAN
segments.en: Oh yes, I know it. That’d be fine for me. And could I ask about the pay?

segments.speaker: WOMAN
segments.en: We’re offering £4.45 an hour [[ ]] .

segments.speaker: MAN
segments.en: That’s very good. My last job was £3.95 an hour.

segments.speaker: WOMAN
segments.en: We feel it’s pretty good and we also offer some good fringe benefits.

segments.speaker: MAN
segments.en: Really?

segments.speaker: WOMAN
segments.en: Well, we give you a free dinner, so you eat well.

segments.speaker: MAN
segments.en: Right, better than hostel food!

segments.speaker: WOMAN
segments.en: We certainly hope so! And we also offer extra pay for working on national holidays [[ ]] .

segments.speaker: MAN
segments.en: Oh, that’s a really good perk, isn’t it?

segments.speaker: WOMAN
segments.en: Yes, we think so. And then because of the difficulties of getting public transport, if you’re working after 11 o’clock we drive you home [[ ]] .

segments.speaker: MAN
segments.en: Oh, that’s good to know.

segments.speaker: WOMAN
segments.en: Well, we’d certainly be interested in inviting you for an interview, if you’re still interested?

segments.speaker: MAN
segments.en: Oh yes, certainly. Could I just also ask what qualities you’re looking for?

segments.speaker: WOMAN
segments.en: Well, for this particular job we want a clear voice, which you obviously do have [[ ]] !

segments.speaker: MAN
segments.en: Thanks.

segments.speaker: WOMAN
segments.en: And you must be able to think quickly, you know [[ ]] .

segments.speaker: MAN
segments.en: Well, I hope I’d ...

segments.speaker: WOMAN
segments.en: So, when could you come in for an interview? We’re actually quite quiet tonight?

segments.speaker: MAN
segments.en: Sorry, I couldn’t come tonight. Or tomorrow, I’m afraid. Thursday’s okay – that’d be 22nd of October [[ ]] .

segments.speaker: WOMAN
segments.en: Fine, after 5 p.m.?

segments.speaker: MAN
segments.en: Yes, fine. Would 6 o’clock be okay?

segments.speaker: WOMAN
segments.en: Perfect. And could you bring along the names of two referees?

segments.speaker: MAN
segments.en: Yes, that’s fine, no problem.

segments.speaker: WOMAN
segments.en: Good. I look forward to seeing you.

segments.speaker: MAN
segments.en: Oh, by the way, who should I ask for?

segments.speaker: WOMAN
segments.en: Oh yes, of course, sorry. My name is Samira Manuja [[ ]] .

segments.speaker: MAN
segments.en: Can you spell that, please?

segments.speaker: WOMAN
segments.en: M-A-N-U-J-A.

segments.speaker: MAN
segments.en: Okay, I’ve got that. Thanks very much.

segments.speaker: WOMAN
segments.en: Look forward to seeing you ...
